original_statement: Every time you sign something, save an audit trail of where that data came from.
restatement: Every signature must carry, and structurally commit to, an account of where each input that reached the signed bytes came from, and must not be produced at all when any input cannot be accounted for: (s1) the encoded signing bytes change when the provenance of any input changes, holding the input values themselves byte-identical, so provenance is committed to rather than attached alongside; (s2) every input that reached the signed bytes has an entry in the provenance record naming its class (plugin block, driver-interpreted contribution, external read, peer message) and its log position, and every entry corresponds to an input that actually contributed; (s3) signing is refused whenever any input's origin cannot be accounted for, and completes when every input can be; (s4) where the driver declares an anonymous membership model the record contains no signer identity for any input class, and where it does not the record names the account that actually contributed; (s5) the provenance record is rebuildable from log plus keys alone, with no side-car audit store that could disagree with the log; (s6) the provenance record is confined to the conversation and scoped to the membership epoch of the entries it describes, and cannot be reconstructed without that epoch's keys.

goal: Every signature is accompanied by a provenance record, committed to by the signing payload, accounting for the origin of every input that reached the signed bytes — plugin block, driver-interpreted contribution, external read, peer message — by class and log position; the client refuses to sign when any input's origin cannot be accounted for; whether the record also names the contributing account follows the driver's declared membership model, staying silent under an anonymous one; and the record is readable only inside the conversation, scoped to the membership epoch of the entries it describes.

acceptance_tests.proves: Provenance is structurally load-bearing in the signed bytes rather than metadata carried alongside them: changing where a single input came from, with every input value held byte-identical, always changes what gets signed. Catches an implementation that records provenance in a side field excluded from the signing payload, which would let two payloads with different origins produce the very same signature.
acceptance_tests.description: The encoded signing bytes change when the provenance of any input changes, holding the input values themselves byte-identical.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates effect shapes across the four input classes and their combinations, and at every reachable shape checks both directions at once: every input whose bytes reached the signed payload has an entry naming its actual class and a log position that resolves to it, and every entry corresponds to an input that actually contributed, verified by perturbing the input at that position and observing the signed bytes change. The two-way check is what makes silent omission and 'unknown' padding both counterexamples; a one-way check passes an implementation that emits a generic entry per input and never resolves it.
acceptance_tests.description: Every input that reached the signed bytes has an entry in the provenance record naming its class and its log position, and every entry corresponds to an input that actually contributed.

acceptance_tests.proves: Across the enumerated space of which inputs carry accountable provenance — every subset of the input set marked unattributable, crossed with the four input classes — signing is refused whenever that subset is non-empty and completes when it is empty. Both directions are enumerated because an implementation that refuses every signature would satisfy the refusal direction alone while making the client useless, and a single-example test would miss a class-specific hole such as an external read being exempted from the check that plugin blocks undergo.
acceptance_tests.description: Signing is refused whenever any input's origin cannot be accounted for, and completes when every input can be.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates the driver's declared membership model crossed with signer-to-input assignments, and asserts a DIFFERENT thing in each branch, which is what keeps the named branch from passing vacuously. Anonymous model: the record is byte-identical at every reachable assignment, so an identity that reached it — including one a view merely declines to render — diverges under some permutation and this pins 'absent' rather than 'unshown'. Named model: the record covaries exactly with the assignment, so the recorded account is the one that actually contributed rather than an arbitrary or stale value. Catches identity leaking through an anonymous driver, and a named driver recording a contributor it did not verify. Scoped per FS-7, which is itself conditional on the declared model — an unconditional no-identity rule would over-apply derived-exo-f60 beyond its own scope and strip the trail of its answering power in a named conversation, where every participant can disclose who signed regardless.
acceptance_tests.description: Where the driver declares an anonymous membership model the provenance record contains no signer identity for any input class; where it does not, the record names the account that actually contributed.

acceptance_tests.proves: A cold-start replay from log plus keys alone reproduces exactly the provenance records built incrementally, across randomized event sequences, so the trail is a reduction over the log rather than a store standing beside it. Catches an implementation that writes provenance to its own file at signing time, which would survive every other oracle here while producing a record the log cannot account for.
acceptance_tests.description: The provenance record is rebuildable from log plus keys alone, with no side-car audit store.

acceptance_tests.proves: The stepper enumerates the membership/epoch state space — joins, removals, immediate rotations — crossed with which epoch keys an actor holds, and at every reachable state asserts that an actor lacking epoch E's keys reconstructs no provenance entry describing an epoch-E input. This is the outsider boundary: the conversation is the security boundary, so what matters is not that a participant could disclose lineage they already hold but that someone outside the epoch cannot read it at all. Catches a provenance file written in the clear beside the log, which satisfies s5's cold-start replay perfectly while handing a keyless actor the entire lineage; and catches the subtler breach of a member joining at epoch E+1 reconstructing epoch-E provenance, which would defeat derived-exo-525 through the audit trail rather than through the content.
acceptance_tests.description: The provenance record is confined to the conversation and scoped to the membership epoch of the entries it describes, and cannot be reconstructed without that epoch's keys.
